items.source_title: No Dumb Questions: What is the AI bottleneck? How does context engineering fix it?
items.short_factual_summary: Stack Overflow frames the current AI adoption bottleneck as missing work context, tool connectivity, human judgment loops, and context distraction rather than model capability alone.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Useful for local practice guidance on context architecture: teams should inventory relevant and irrelevant sources, design rejection of distracting context, test context selection with mock workflows, and treat human approval as part of the workflow design.
items.local_practice_implication: Record as a practice-level source for source selection, context filtering, connector setup cost, and adoption tradeoff analysis.
follow_up_notes: Consider whether a durable local leaf should distinguish context completeness from context distraction during ingest.

items.source_title: Claude Opus 5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
items.short_factual_summary: GitHub added Claude Opus 5 to Copilot surfaces and highlighted early testing on autonomous code changes, regression verification, coordinated tool use, targeted changes, and reduced execution overhead.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The practice signal is model selection by task shape: long-running coding tasks need explicit regression verification and overhead tracking, while administrators still control model availability through policy.
items.local_practice_implication: Use only as a downstream note about model-policy gating, regression-verification expectations, and agentic task-fit evaluation.
follow_up_notes: Route broad model/product coverage upstream if ingested.

items.source_title: GitHub Mobile: Fix failing Actions checks with Copilot cloud agent
items.short_factual_summary: GitHub Mobile now lets users ask Copilot coding agent to investigate a failed GitHub Actions check, open a new pull request on top of the existing pull request, and tag the user for review.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Shows a concrete CI-to-agent repair loop where the agent proposes a separate reviewable PR instead of mutating the original branch directly.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate evidence for regression repair handoff patterns, especially preserving review boundaries around agent fixes.
follow_up_notes: Check whether existing source-workflow leaves already cover PR-on-PR repair handoff before creating a new local lens.

items.source_title: Copilot cloud agent for Linear is now generally available
items.short_factual_summary: The Linear integration lets teams assign issues to Copilot cloud agent, which opens a draft pull request in an ephemeral GitHub Actions environment, streams progress to Linear, requests review, and supports model choice, custom agents, branch controls, and steering comments.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Strong local signal for issue-to-agent handoff contracts: task assignment, base/working branch control, progress streaming, custom repository agents, and review request are explicit workflow surfaces.
items.local_practice_implication: Capture as downstream evidence for governed background-agent workflows and structured issue handoff controls.
follow_up_notes: Could update an existing issue-to-agent handoff or streaming progress leaf during ingest.

items.source_title: Agent automation controls in GitHub Issues in public preview
items.date_basis: Changelog page shows July 23, 2026 and an editor note on July 24, 2026.
items.short_factual_summary: GitHub Issues added public-preview controls for agent automations: approvals, confidence levels, and rationale on supported changes to labels, fields, issue type, closure, and assignees. The page explicitly says approvals are workflow convenience, not a security control.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: This is directly relevant to local governance semantics: confidence-rated suggestions, rationale-bearing audit trails, and the difference between review convenience and enforceable security boundary.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate for a local approval-boundary or agent-rationale leaf because the source distinguishes lifecycle review from security enforcement.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, avoid presenting approvals as permission controls.

items.source_title: GitHub MCP Server supports the next MCP specification
items.short_factual_summary: GitHub MCP Server added support for the next MCP specification before its July 28, 2026 release, including stateless core changes, removed sessions/initialize behavior, header-based logging and secret-scanning support, elicitation changes, and official conformance tests.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Local practice implication is governed MCP upgrade handling: stateless transport changes, logging without payload inspection, elicitation compatibility, and conformance suites as agent-verifiable implementation gates.
items.local_practice_implication: Record as a downstream governed-tooling practice note, not an upstream MCP server product leaf.
follow_up_notes: Potentially relevant to existing governed MCP gateway and conformance-test verification pages.

items.date_basis: Anthropic newsroom and article page show Jul 24, 2026.
items.short_factual_summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5 and beta API features for mid-conversation tool changes without invalidating prompt cache and automatic fallbacks for safety-classifier-blocked requests.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: The local practice signal is runtime tool-surface management: changing tools mid-conversation affects cache and permission design, while fallback routing should be governed and auditable when safety classifiers alter execution paths.
items.local_practice_implication: Possible downstream lens for tool-list mutation, prompt-cache assumptions, and fallback routing governance.
follow_up_notes: Route broad model release facts upstream; keep only tool-change and fallback governance implications locally.

items.source_title: Tencent WorkBuddy Bench: A Multi-Domain Coding-Agent Benchmark with Contamination-Resistant Task Construction
items.date_basis: arXiv abstract page shows submitted on 23 Jul 2026 and v1 Thu, 23 Jul 2026 04:34:06 UTC.
items.short_factual_summary: The paper introduces an open multi-domain coding-agent benchmark spanning repository code, web front-end work, office workflows, and security workflows, with tasks reverse-engineered from real work but rewritten to resist prompt contamination and scored under reproducible harnesses.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Useful local evidence for eval design: benchmark tasks should be distribution-informed, auditable, contamination-resistant, workspace-shaped, and scored with domain-specific verifiers rather than a single aggregate score.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate evidence for software-engineering eval pages and harness architecture guidance.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, keep benchmark entity background upstream if needed and focus local writing on eval methodology.

items.source_title: Maintenance Signals in AI-Assisted GitHub Repositories: Evidence from GenAI Adopters
items.date_basis: arXiv abstract page shows submitted on 23 Jul 2026 and v1 Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:10:10 UTC.
items.short_factual_summary: The paper studies 622 public GenAI adopters, 179 repositories with visible AI-assistance configuration files, matched traditional repositories, and 248 AI-assisted-repository issues, finding signals that AI assistance shifts maintenance work toward validating generated content, external AI dependencies, and AI-specific behavior.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Good evidence that adoption operating models should track maintenance and validation work, not just code generation velocity.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate source for team adoption and coding-practice pages that discuss repository maintenance overhead from AI assistance.
follow_up_notes: Check whether existing adoption pages have a maintenance-cost lens before adding new coverage.

items.source_title: Delivery, Not Storage: Cue-Anchored Working Memory as a Harness Property for Coding Agents
items.date_basis: arXiv abstract page shows submitted on 23 Jul 2026 and v1 Thu, 23 Jul 2026 06:50:04 UTC.
items.short_factual_summary: The paper argues that coding-agent memory must be harness-delivered rather than voluntarily retrieved by the agent, proposing cue-triggered memory injection based on paths, symbols, events, semantics, and time, with audit-logged deterministic delivery.
items.why_it_matters_for_ai_assisted_developme: Strong local signal for durable agent instructions and context architecture: memory delivery, provenance framing, staleness checks, and post-compaction re-injection are harness responsibilities, not prompt-only obligations.
items.local_practice_implication: Candidate source for context-continuity and harness-owned memory pages.
follow_up_notes: During ingest, separate the general technique/entity background from local practice claims about deterministic delivery and audit logs.
